item.title: What's Coming in C++26: Reflection, Contracts, and the Biggest Standard Update in Years
item.description: Every C++ standard since C++11 has been “the incremental one” — C++17 tidied things up, C++20 gave us concepts and coroutines, C++23 was mostly cleanup. C++26 is different. Two features landing in it — static reflection and contracts — have been on the wishlist since before C++11 shipped, and they’re finally real. I went through the accepted papers and current compiler support to figure out what actually changes for people writing C++ day to day, not just what sounds impressive on a slide.

item.title: C++ vs Rust vs Go in 2026: Which One Should You Actually Learn?
item.description: Every few months someone asks me the same question: “should I learn Rust or just stick with C++?” Lately Go gets thrown into that question too. I’ve written a lot of C++, poked at Rust, and shipped small things in Go — so here’s my honest 2026 take, backed by what’s actually happening in the ecosystem right now, not vibes. Why this comparison actually matters in 2026 This isn’t an academic exercise.
